claims.statement: The `brijio` binary is the single entry point that starts both the WebSocket server (default port 8787) and MCP HTTP server (default port 8788) in one process and also owns the daemon lifecycle, --print-config, --doctor, and --dev commands; a legacy `browserbridge` binary alias points at the same module and emits a deprecation warning.

parseDaemonCommand dispatches argv into a typed DaemonCommand; --dev is extracted before subcommand parsing so it combines with run args, and unknown args that are not recognized subcommands fall through to run mode preserving any server-level flags.

loadBrijioEnv resolves .env from the first existing candidate in priority order: BRIJIO_ENV_FILE, then cwd/.env, then ~/.brijio/.env; applyBrijioEnv copies loaded values into process.env only when the existing env var is unset or empty, so explicit environment wins over file values.

The entry point auto-generates BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN (accepting BROWSERBRIDGE_PAIRING_TOKEN and BRIJIO_TOKEN aliases) and MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN via crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') when unset, mirrors the resolved pairing token to both new and legacy env var names, and the MCP HTTP server throws if MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN is empty.

Default hosts/ports are applied just before server startup (WEBSOCKET_HOST 0.0.0.0, WEBSOCKET_PORT 8787, MCP_HTTP_HOST 0.0.0.0, MCP_HTTP_PORT 8788, MCP_HTTP_PATH /mcp); --dev and demo override both hosts to 127.0.0.1, and demo also binds the static demo page server to 0.0.0.0 so it is reachable via Tailscale/LAN.
Server modules are imported dynamically only when run/demo mode is actually reached; --doctor and --print-config exit before that import cascade so they never load the full server stack.

In demo mode the entry point probes http://127.0.0.1:<wsPort>/health; if a daemon is already running it starts only the demo page server and sets demoAttachedToExistingDaemon so the banner omits WS/MCP URLs and tokens that belong to the daemon process.

install writes persistent OS-managed service definitions under ~/.brijio/ for darwin (launchd) and linux (systemd); other platforms throw from normalizePlatform. It creates ~/.brijio and bin/, writes a shell wrapper, generates tokens into ~/.brijio/.env chmod 0600, and applies --ws-port/--mcp-port overrides while preserving existing values.

Tokens are never embedded in the service definitions: the macOS launchd plist has no EnvironmentVariables and the Linux systemd unit references EnvironmentFile=%h/.brijio/.env; planDaemonInstall writes tokens only to ~/.brijio/.env (chmod 0600). A test asserts the systemd unit contains no token value.

install is idempotent: if .env already exists, existing BRIJIO_PAIRING_TOKEN and MCP_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN are preserved and only absent values are generated; passing new --ws-port/--mcp-port overrides those ports in .env while omitting a flag leaves the existing port intact.

The macOS launchd plist sets RunAtLoad true, KeepAlive true, WorkingDirectory ~/.brijio, and routes both stdout and stderr to ~/.brijio/brijio.log; the Linux systemd unit uses Type=simple, Restart=on-failure (not always), EnvironmentFile=%h/.brijio/.env, and WantedBy=default.target.

uninstall stops/disables the daemon and removes the service symlink but preserves ~/.brijio/ config and logs, printing a note for full removal; start/stop/restart wrap launchctl load/unload (macOS) or systemctl --user start|stop|restart brijio.service (Linux) and never modify .env.

status loads the env to resolve ports, checks the daemon loaded state via launchctl list (macOS) or systemctl --user is-active (linux), probes both WS and MCP health endpoints, and returns a DaemonStatus formatted by formatStatus into a table.
logs tails ~/.brijio/brijio.log (macOS) or journalctl --user -u brijio.service (Linux); --live/-n and --lines/-n control the initial line count, with --live following the log stream.

brijio --doctor runs runDoctorChecks and formatDoctorReport, starts no servers, and exits 1 if any check is fail. Checks: config (pass if found/readable, warn if no path or missing), MCP HTTP and WebSocket ports (pass if listenable, fail with EADDRINUSE guidance), network detection (pass listing Tailscale/mDNS/localhost signals, warn on error), and Node.js (fail below v18).

detectNetworkPaths probes Tailscale via `tailscale status --json` (2s timeout) preferring the first 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT address, falls back to detectTailscaleInterface scanning os.networkInterfaces() for a 100.64.0.0/10 IPv4, and detects mDNS by resolving <hostname>.local via dns.resolve; bestHost priority is Tailscale > mDNS > 127.0.0.1.

--print-config prints a ready-to-copy MCP client config block to stdout with a where-to-paste hint to stderr so `brijio --print-config <agent> > config.json` yields a clean file; it resolves mcpUrl/wsUrl from the config pipeline plus detectNetworkPaths().bestHost unless --dev forces 127.0.0.1.

Twelve agents are supported by --print-config via resolveAgentName (case-insensitive, with aliases): claude-desktop/claude, cursor/cur, vscode/vs, cline, codex, hermes, claude-code/code, gemini, windsurf, zed, continue, and goose. Each has a pure formatter in print-config.ts / print-config-commands.ts; without an agent it shows an interactive numbered prompt when stdin is a TTY, else falls back to the widest-compatible mcpServers JSON.

The CLI-based agents codex, claude-code, and gemini emit shell commands rather than config files; codex uses --bearer-token-env-var (referencing the env var name, not a literal token) while claude-code and gemini embed the literal Authorization Bearer header; goose prints an instructional not-supported message because Goose is stdio-only and Brijio is HTTP-only.

formatStartupBanner writes to stderr so stdout stays clean for piping; when dev is false it calls detectNetworkPaths() best-effort and lists all reachable Local/Tailscale/mDNS addresses with WS and MCP URLs, when dev is true it forces 127.0.0.1 and skips detection; it annotates auto-generated tokens with [ephemeral] and in demoAttachedToExistingDaemon mode prints only the demo page URL.

Per ADR-0033 both servers expose GET /health and emit single-line JSON logs to stderr via createLogger from @brijio/shared (packages/shared/src/logger.ts) with no external logging dependency; the WS health returns status/version/uptimeSeconds/extensions (count + browser IDs), the MCP health returns status/version/uptimeSeconds/websocket (url + status unknown), and the MCP /health route is handled before auth/path checks.

docker-compose.yml defines three profiles: runtime (the brijio service exposing WS and MCP ports with env interpolation), legacy-runtime (a browserbridge service extending brijio), and test (an nginx test-page service serving clients/test-page on TEST_PAGE_PORT default 8080).
